The petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 3 in C.C.No.319 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kunnamangalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offences alleged against them are under Sections 406 and 498A read with Section 34 of the IPC.
The offence relates to the matrimonial cruelty perpetrated upon the defacto complainant by the 1st petitioner along with the other petitioners, who are his close relatives.
2. In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that the issue has been amicably settled with the defacto complainant, who had sworn an affidavit to that effect.
3. Earlier, a counsel had appeared for the defacto complainant.
Today, when the matter is taken up for consideration, the learned counsel, who represented the defacto complainant, submitted that he is relinquishing the vakalat.

The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions from the Investigating Officer, submitted that the defacto complainant had given a statement to the Investigating Officer to the effect that she is now not amenable for any settlement, though she had sworn an affidavit consenting for a settlement of issue between the parties.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
6. The petitioners seek to quash the criminal proceedings against them on the basis of the compromise said to have been arrived with the defacto complainant.

Though it is seen that an affidavit purportedly sworn by the defacto complainant has been brought on record, as per the instructions received by the learned Public Prosecutor from the Investigating Officer, the defacto complainant had given a statement to the Investigating Officer to the effect that she is not amenable for any settlement.
Coupled with that, the learned counsel representing the defacto complainant has now submitted that he is relinquishing the vakalat of the defacto complainant.

In that view of the matter, it is not possible to proceed with the question as to whether the criminal prosecution launched 2025:KER:72717 against the petitioners are liable to be quashed on the basis of the settlement of the issue between the parties, since the defacto complainant has not made it clear as to the compromise said to have been arrived at with the accused.
In the above circumstances, the present Crl.M.C. stands dismissed.

However, it is made clear that the dismissal of this Crl.M.C. will not be a bar for the institution of a fresh petition, if actually the parties arrived at a consensus for the settlement of the issues between them.
